intro.text: A Kholin lord and uncle of King Elhokar, fighting in the Alethi war on the Shattered Plains, who suffers strange visions during every highstorm.
Highprince of War under his nephew King Elhokar, who traded away his Shardblade to free Sadeas's bridgemen and strives to live by the old Alethi Codes of War.
An Alethi highprince who bonded the Stormfather and became a Bondsmith, leading the surviving armies to the ancient tower city of Urithiru to prepare for the Everstorm.
A Bondsmith and the leader of a coalition of nations and Knights Radiant against Odium, who gave up his authority in Alethkar so that his niece Jasnah could rule it as queen.

story.text: During every highstorm Dalinar fell into fits, living through visions of the past as if he were there. Believing the visions came from the Almighty, often featuring the Knights Radiant as heroes, he took them as a command to unite the Alethi highprinces. The visions unsettled his family, who kept him hidden away during storms.

Frustrated that the highprinces now competed for gemhearts rather than seeking vengeance, Dalinar joined a hunt with Elhokar and Sadeas in 1173. When a chasmfiend attacked and the king was in danger, Dalinar risked his own life to protect his nephew, the last piece of his brother that he had left.

Dalinar suggested to Elhokar that the Alethi leave the Shattered Plains and asked to be named Highprince of War, but the king refused unless the highprinces could prove they could work together. After a cut girth strap suggested an attempt on Elhokar's life, the king instead named Sadeas Highprince of Information to investigate.

Dalinar confided to Adolin his wish to return to Alethkar, which shocked his son. Adolin already worried for his father's sanity and questioned trusting such blasphemous dreams, but Dalinar insisted the visions were real.

Born around 1120 as the second son of the Kholin family, Dalinar lost his mother young and was raised mostly by a parshman nurse. He got along better with his grandparents than with his father. He admired, and at times envied, his older brother Gavilar, and followed him into the war to unite Alethkar under the Kholin banner.

After Alethkar was united, Gavilar lost his taste for battle and began urging peace and the Codes of War from a book called The Way of Kings. Dalinar resisted, and in 1166 talked him into a chasmfiend hunt near the Shattered Plains to rekindle his spirit. There Dalinar met a Parshendi patrol and realized these parshmen were intelligent and organized; he brought Gavilar to meet them, and the two peoples soon learned to communicate.

Having lost the Thrill in battle, Dalinar began to question why the war was being fought and whether peace with the Parshendi might be better, though he kept this to himself since the highprinces saw such ideas as weakness. When eight highprinces refused joint assaults, leaving only Sadeas, he told Navani he was considering abdicating to Adolin; she urged him to stay.

Navani recognized the gibberish Dalinar spoke during his fits as the Dawnchant, a long-dead language he could not have known, proving the visions real. Reassured, he grew certain that his task was to unite the princes and that he could trust Sadeas.

During the assault at the Tower, Dalinar, Adolin and the Kholin army had all but resigned themselves to death when Kaladin and Bridge Four returned and gave them a way off the plateau. Dalinar promised to free the bridgemen from Sadeas, and they returned to the warcamp to confront him.

Dalinar blamed himself for Gavilar's assassination, believing he had failed to follow the Codes of War that night. Since then he has kept the Codes zealously, believing they stop a man from becoming what he loathes, and that a leader should never order his men to do what he would not do himself.
Tired of being manipulated, Dalinar pressed Elhokar into naming him Highprince of War, and told his nephew that he was now in a relationship with Navani, the king's mother.

When Sadeas would not sell the bridgemen, Dalinar traded his Shardblade, Oathbringer, for them. He made Kaladin captain of the freed bridgemen, named Bridge Four his family's honor guard, and gave Kaladin his cloak. He also gave his Shardplate to Renarin.

Dalinar realized he had misread the visions: they were recordings, not conversations. The Almighty had not told him specifically to unite Alethkar or trust Sadeas, and in the last vision declared that he was dead, killed by Odium.
As Highprince of War, Dalinar began planning to unify Alethkar and refound the Knights Radiant. Soon after his next vision, he found glyphs scratched into his wall: Sixty-two days. Death follows.

Dalinar commanded the respect of the highprinces' meetings, acting like a king even with Elhokar present. He approached Highprince Aladar in person, reminding him of what happened to a highprince who once resisted unification and offering advice that won Aladar's battle, but Aladar still refused to join him.

Kaladin told Dalinar that Amaram had stolen a Shardblade Kaladin won and sold him into slavery. Amaram was an old friend whom Dalinar considered honorable, so he asked for proof. After another attempt on Elhokar's life, Dalinar warned the king of more assassins and of something worse: the Everstorm.

The Assassin in White, Szeth, came for Dalinar during a highstorm and easily held off Dalinar, Adolin and Kaladin. Dalinar caught Szeth's falling Blade between his palms, giving Kaladin time to tackle the assassin out of the palace. Judging the assassin unstoppable, Dalinar proposed going to the Parshendi to make peace or defeat them.

Dalinar visited Kaladin in prison and told him he would be released soon. He explained some of Elhokar's decisions and advised Kaladin that the only way to change things was to become a leader beyond reproach.

With days left before the predicted storm, Dalinar sought allies for an expedition into the Plains but was mostly mocked; only Roion, Sebarial and Aladar joined him. Visiting an injured Kaladin, he wondered whether Kaladin was the one he had been waiting for. He tested Amaram and confirmed Kaladin's story, but was forced to let him go.

On the march, Shallan revealed her Lightweaving to Dalinar, and he offered her leadership of the Radiants, which she declined. Shen, a Parshendi spy who had served in Bridge Four, surrendered and warned that the Parshendi had been replaced by their ancient gods. When he said their song must be stopped, Dalinar ordered an immediate attack.

In the battle, Dalinar heard the voice from his visions while awake for the first time. It said it was not the Almighty but a sliver of him left behind, that it was sorry Dalinar would die there, and that the visions were over.

As the army evacuated, Szeth appeared again, killed Roion, and Lashed Dalinar high into the sky. Kaladin caught him with his new Windrunner powers and brought him safely down, and Dalinar knew Kaladin was what he had been looking for.

Shallan's Oathgate carried the army to Urithiru. On the tower's roof Dalinar called on the Stormfather, who resented humanity and had no hope for him, and demanded a bond until the spren grudgingly agreed, making him a Bondsmith. He warned Kaladin, Shallan and Renarin that the Everstorm would transform the parshmen into Voidbringers.

Bonded to the Stormfather, Dalinar revisited the visions freely and saw a figure in dark Shardplate with red eyes and nine shadows, which the Stormfather named the Unmade and Odium's champion. Convinced he needed an alliance of Roshar's rulers, he began reaching out to them.

When Sadeas was found murdered in Urithiru, Dalinar privately saw it as something to celebrate and used the moment to delegate: Aladar became Highprince of Information to police the tower, Sebarial Highprince of Commerce to build its markets, and Adolin took charge of the troops, while the Radiants were given Stormlight to practice.

In his youth, during the war of unification, Dalinar picked an elite force, sometimes recruiting enemies. When Teleb shot him with black arrows from an astonishing distance, Dalinar chased him down and recruited him, and the incident earned Dalinar the name Blackthorn. He followed Gavilar's orders blindly, attacking Yezriar's princedom without knowing why.

Feeling the enemy in the Everstorm, Dalinar admitted to Navani that he could not hear his late wife's name or remember her, since he had gone to the Nightwatcher. With no ardent willing to marry them, he asked the Stormfather, who appeared to all and received their vows. His ardent Kadash confronted him over this heresy, stirring vague memories of Rathalas.

While studying maps, Dalinar's and Shallan's powers combined to create a map of the world in Stormlight. Dalinar decided to focus on protecting cities with Oathgates, especially Thaylenah, Azir and Jah Keved. After a second, copycat murder, he assigned Adolin to the investigation of Sadeas's death.

In the past, Dalinar won Shardplate, then attacked Rathalas, the Rift, to take Brightlord Tanalan's Blade. He defeated Tanalan and tracked the Blade to Tanalan's widow and young son, but could not bring himself to kill them. Gavilar told him the Blade was Oathbringer, once owned by the conqueror Sadees the Sunmaker.

Dalinar's appeals to other monarchs met little success: the Azish falsely claimed their Oathgate was broken, and Queen Fen of Thaylenah refused any coalition. Elhokar then swore fealty to Dalinar, making him Highking of Urithiru with Adolin as heir to his princedom, and planned to retake Kholinar through its Oathgate with Kaladin's help.

Studying an Honorblade, Dalinar asked the Stormfather whether Odium could be bound by oaths, and considered proposing a contest of champions to buy humanity time. With his ardents unwilling to spar with a heretic, he wrestled one of General Khal's sons and lost.

In the past, as the war slowed, the Kholins sought allies in Rira and Iri, negotiating with the Westerner Toh and his sister Evi. Dalinar impressed them by strolling through a highstorm and casually stopping an assassin from killing Gavilar.

The Iriali queen announced Iri would side with the Voidbringers unless Adolin's Shardplate was returned. When Navani noted that Adolin inherited the Plate from his mother, Evi, Dalinar heard her name for the first time since the Nightwatcher, and over the following days many memories of her returned.

Taravangian arrived as the first monarch to visit, introducing a new Radiant, Malata. Reviewing his failed diplomacy, Dalinar realized that when Taravangian asked whom they would attack next, everyone expected the Blackthorn to conquer, and he began to rethink his approach and his Bondsmith oaths.

In the past, betrothed to Evi, Dalinar attacked Highprince Kalanor and was so lost in the Thrill that he killed his own men. He won Kalanor's Shards in a duel, then turned on Gavilar, stopping only when his brother removed his helm and smiled. Ashamed, he gave Gavilar the Shards and swore he must never be king.

In a war council, Dalinar warned that the enemy was seizing cities with Oathgates. Ialai Sadeas then arrived with Amaram and named him the new Highprince Sadeas; after Elhokar approved, Dalinar accepted it, holding back an enraged Adolin.

Azir sealed its Oathgate and Fen again refused him. When Oathbringer was found in a planter in the tower, Dalinar returned it to Ialai, telling her he had not killed her husband. Amaram called him a hypocrite, and he spent the evening discussing morality and the Hogman's Murder from The Way of Kings with Taravangian.

Dalinar told the Stormfather that a hypocrite may simply be someone who is changing. Learning that the Stormfather could bring anyone touching him or caught in a highstorm into the visions, he saw a new way to reach the other monarchs.

Dalinar brought Fen into the Starfalls vision. She called him a tyrant and murderer; frustrated, he shouted that she had no choice but to stand with him. Fen, unfazed and even pleased, said the man on the spanreed was not the Blackthorn she knew, and agreed to reconsider.

In the past, Dalinar married Evi and the war of unification formally ended. Their love was strained by her horror at his killing. When Rathalas demanded the return of Oathbringer to Tanalan's heir, Evi was glad he had spared the boy, while Dalinar was glad of the chance for more fighting.

In a vision of the Last Desolation with Navani and Jasnah, Dalinar demanded the truth, and the Stormfather explained the Oathpact, the Heralds' abandonment of Talenel, and that the madman who came to Kholinar was Taln himself. He refused to reveal the secret behind the Recreance, fearing the Radiants would break their oaths.

Dalinar brought the young Azish emperor, Yanagawn, into a vision and tried to convince him that he was different from his ancestor Sadees. To the Stormfather's shock, Lift entered the vision, told the emperor not to trust Dalinar, and took him away.

In the past, kept at home in Kholinar, Dalinar grew restless, using firemoss and maiming men in tavern fights. Summoned from a wrestling match when Evi went into labor, he was overjoyed at his son, naming him Adolin and hoping he would have his father's strength and his mother's compassion.

Flown by Kaladin's Windrunners, Dalinar inspected the old warcamps and received word that Fen would visit Urithiru. At the monastery he found the madman's cell cut open with a Shardblade and a poisoned dart left behind.

In the past, Gavilar sent Dalinar to fight Herdazians and Vedens on the border instead of Rathalas. Over four years he became his brother's best general. Evi brought Adolin and their second son, Renarin, to the front; Dalinar disliked the boy's name, and was troubled by how long the Thrill lingered even with his family.

In the Highway to the Sun vision, Dalinar gave Yanagawn and his viziers what knowledge he could. As the others faded, Odium appeared. He said he would destroy Cultivation and Honor's remnants if freed, declined a contest of champions, and showed Dalinar a glimpse of his true, overwhelming self.

In storm-ravaged Thaylen City, Dalinar learned he must be a diplomat. To show he was no conqueror, he let a young Thaylen soldier stab him, then felt ashamed of the Blackthorn's bullying. Hearing the broken stones of a temple, he used his Bondsmith powers to fuse it whole again, and convinced Fen to join his coalition.

The Stormfather told Dalinar he held the powers of Ishar, Binder of Gods, and that there were only three Bondsmith spren. Dalinar gave the Honorblade to Bridge Four for training, then went to Azimir with essays from Fen, Navani and Jasnah.

In Azimir, Dalinar used Connection to understand Azish. Navani's sincere essay persuaded the Azish and several allied nations to join. As he left, a vizier remarked that he was less savage than expected; Dalinar said he had changed, and memories of Evi and the Rift flooded back, making him collapse on returning to Urithiru.

In the past, as Adolin joined him on campaign, Dalinar tried to be a better man for his son. Then Gavilar sent him to put down the rebellion at the Rift. Dalinar was pleased, but Evi wept at the prospect of endless war, and he promised her a year in Kholinar once it was done.

In the past, hoping to spare Evi pain, Dalinar met the younger Tanalan, the boy he had spared, now Brightlord of the Rift. They worked out a face-saving peace, promising Tanalan a highprinceship, and Tanalan warned that Sadeas was working against Dalinar and told him where Sadeas's men were hiding.

In the past, ambushed and badly injured, Dalinar slaughtered his attackers in a rage of the Thrill and staggered back to camp. Ignoring Evi's plea for peace and agreeing with Sadeas that the Rift must pay, he had Soulcasters make oil, sent Evi away, and vowed to turn the city into a pyre.

In the past, within hours, Evi's body was recovered where Tanalan had said it would be. Though it looked as if she had tried to defect, Dalinar made sure no one called her a traitor, refused to admit his own responsibility, and told his people she had died a hero and that he had burned the Rift in retribution.

After eight days shut away with his memories, Dalinar emerged to await news from Kholinar, asking the Stormfather and Taravangian how anyone could live with such deeds. Word then came that the mission to Kholinar had failed, with no news of Elhokar, Kaladin, Shallan or Adolin.
In the past, haunted by the screams of Evi and the people of Rathalas, Dalinar turned to drink. His drinking became so serious that his family hid alcohol from him and he begged it from strangers.

In the past, the expedition that discovered the Parshendi made Dalinar feel more himself than he had in the decade since the Rift. Back in Kholinar, still drinking, he was angry and distant with his sons, until Renarin's unfailing love broke through and Dalinar realized he had to stop hating them for reminding him of Evi.

Still haunted, Dalinar let Navani lead the coalition's first meeting and went to assess Vedenar. There he felt the Thrill for the first time in years and realized it had left him rather than been overcome. Fleeing it, he was met by ardents who declared him excommunicated, and forced the Oathgate to work without a Shardblade.

Back in Urithiru, hearing Evi's voice telling him to accept who he was, Dalinar found The Way of Kings no help. He took a bottle of wine from Adolin's room and began drinking again, preferring that to killing.

After three days of drinking, Dalinar dreamed of Nohadon, who took him shopping for bread and told him that hypocrisy can mean a person is changing. When a thunderclast appeared, Nohadon stilled it. Dalinar awoke and remembered Gavilar's funeral.

In the past, at Gavilar's funeral, Dalinar sent Adolin to swear the Vengeance Pact while he went to drink, but heard Jasnah reading The Way of Kings and asked her to continue. She read it all to him. Afterward he told Adolin he had been a poor father but was proud of his sons, and resolved to be better.

Recovered, Dalinar admitted to the coalition that he had abandoned them, and realized the enemy would strike Thaylen City rather than familiar Jah Keved. He refused Fen's request to recant his heresy, offered to release Kadash from serving him, and asked the Stormfather to arrange a meeting with the enemy's leader.

In the vision, Dalinar met Venli, who rejected a truce and said his only hope was to surrender to Odium. Odium then took over the vision, claimed to understand Dalinar's pain, and said peace would come after Dalinar destroyed Roshar. Dalinar could not voice a challenge of champions, and the Stormfather wept from the cost of holding Odium back.

At the coalition meeting in Thaylen City, a translation of the Eila Stele revealed that humans had been the original invaders. Simultaneous leaks about the highking arrangement and Dalinar's meetings with Odium followed, and Dalinar realized he had been outmaneuvered by scholars rather than armies.

The Stormfather revealed this knowledge had caused the Recreance. Bridge Four began leaving, the Azish departed, and Taravangian abandoned him. The Stormfather then accused Dalinar of living a lie for six years, pretending he had not killed Evi.

In the past, traveling separately to the Shattered Plains, Dalinar visited the Nightwatcher. On the way he relived the burning of Rathalas and saw visions of a future of conquest. He asked the Nightwatcher whether he could be forgiven; unable to grant this, she gave way to an older woman she called child, who told him to attend her instead.

In the past, the woman agreed to prune Dalinar rather than change him, warning that the cost was high and that she would also take Evi. He agreed. Afterward he could not recall the bargain, assumed he had been granted peace, and resolved to stop drinking, follow the Codes of War, and read The Way of Kings.

When the Everstorm brought Odium's army to Thaylen City, Dalinar walked out with The Way of Kings. He rejected the Thrill, saw Amaram's soldiers turn with glowing red eyes, and sent Lift after a great ruby the Fused had stolen. Odium appeared and told him their time had come.

Dalinar demanded a contest of champions, and Odium accepted, revealing he intended Dalinar himself as his champion. Odium forced him to relive the Rift, insisting it was not his fault, and drove the Stormfather from his mind. Broken and in agony, Dalinar found a single gloryspren in his fist and spoke one sentence.

Dalinar declared that he, not Odium, had killed the people of Rathalas and Evi, and that he accepted that responsibility. He swore the Third Ideal, grasped the realms, heard Evi forgive him, and named himself Unity, summoning Honor's Perpendicularity. Kaladin, Adolin and Shallan emerged from the light, though Elhokar was gone.

The Perpendicularity filled the field's gems with Stormlight. Surrounded by Radiants and two Heralds, Dalinar sent Renarin to the Oathgate, Shallan to deceive Amaram's men, Jasnah to repair the wall and Lift to bring the stolen ruby, while Kaladin guarded him as he went to confront the Thrill.

Stepping into the red mist of the Thrill, Dalinar realized it was only the primal urge to fight. He accepted it and his past, and using the ruby Lift brought, trapped the Unmade in the gem. Amaram's soldiers collapsed, the Everstorm departed and the enemy sailed away.
Exhausted, Dalinar told Navani the months of painful memories had prepared him to face Odium, gave her the ruby holding Nergaoul to study, and asked her to teach him to read and write.

Taravangian confessed that he had expected Dalinar to fall and had planned to take over the coalition, and that he had sent the Assassin in White to kill Roshar's monarchs. Dalinar, shocked, used Stormlight to send Kaladin after Gavinor.

Dalinar wanted Adolin crowned king of Alethkar, but Adolin confessed to killing Sadeas and refused. Needing to step away from Alethkar to lead the Radiants, Dalinar agreed to Shallan's suggestion that Jasnah become queen. After Adolin and Shallan's wedding, he began writing his memoir, titled Oathbringer, My Glory and My Shame.
Six months after Thaylen City, Dalinar negotiated a treaty with Ral-na, king of the Reshi isle of Relu-na, and his son Talik, using Lopen to reassure them, to give the coalition allies in the north.

Dalinar and Navani met the Fourth Bridge airship, where Dalinar met Kaladin's father, Lirin, and the Herdazian general known as the Mink, promising to evacuate the Mink's troops. When Fused attacked, Dalinar repeatedly opened the Perpendicularity to give the Radiants an advantage. Afterward he told Kaladin to consider stepping away from combat.

Back in Urithiru, Dalinar caught up on tasks, saw Adolin off to Lasting Integrity after an argument over morality, and left Navani to rule the tower while he went to fight in Azir, ignoring her concern that Gavinor was too young for war.

After several months, Odium drew Dalinar into a vision to set the contest's terms: on an agreed day, each would name a willing champion to fight to the death atop Urithiru. If Dalinar's champion won, Alethkar and Herdaz would return to the coalition; if Odium's won, Odium would keep them and Dalinar would serve him as one of the Fused.

Taravangian chose Gavinor as Odium's champion, forcing Dalinar to either kill a defenseless member of his own family or forfeit the contest. Approaching the power of Honor and telling it he understood it, Dalinar Ascended as its new Vessel.
Soon afterward, Dalinar was killed by strong winds and debris while shielding Gavinor, who survived. Renarin indicated that Jasnah would Soulcast his body to stone.

In a final vision with Nohadon, Dalinar found another way. He renounced his oaths, breaking his bond with the Stormfather, giving up Honor's power and cancelling the contest, which freed Odium from Roshar. Taravangian seized Honor's power too, becoming the composite Shard Retribution, now opposed by every Shard in the cosmere as Dalinar intended.

personality.text: A practical man, Dalinar dislikes fancy silks and lace, preferring a plain uniform, and kept his Shardplate unpainted grey. He finds Wit odd and rather dislikes him, but enjoys watching him torment Sadeas.
Dalinar seeks to stay in control at all times, fearing a return to the man he was as the Blackthorn, and dedicates himself single-mindedly to causes and ideals to keep from sliding back.

He values human life above all else; his taste for battle has waned into a love of greatshell hunts, though killing majestic beasts saddens him. He refuses to use bridge crews and thinks of others' safety before his own. He follows the Codes of War zealously and believes a leader should never order what he would not do himself.

An aging, powerfully built man in his fifties, Dalinar has black hair graying at the temples, blue eyes, a clean-shaven, battle-worn face and a nose crooked from a youthful break. His chest and arms are covered in old scars. He wears a sapphire signet ring bearing his house's glyphpair.

Dalinar insists on admitting his past mistakes and taking responsibility for them, seeing that as the first step toward becoming better, and refuses to give up the pain of his memories, ashamed that he once had them removed. He considers himself a hypocrite in the sense of someone still changing.
